context_requirements: Constitutive or inducible NF-kB/IKK activity, often driven by TNF, IL-1, TLR, or oncogenic mutations (e.g., KRAS, BRAF, BCR-ABL).
Expression of IKKbeta (IKBKB) and/or IKKalpha (CHUK) as the drug targets.
Intact NF-kB signaling components (e.g., NEMO, p65) for downstream transcriptional effects.
Proliferating cells with active cell-cycle machinery for anti-proliferative and mitotic effects.
falsifiers: No decrease in NFKBIA, NFKBIB, or NFKBIE expression at 6 h in any responsive line.
No reduction in NF-kB target genes (e.g., BIRC2, CXCL2, IL1B) at 6 h.
No anti-proliferative or apoptotic gene expression changes at 24 h.
Strong upregulation of NF-kB target genes at 6 h, opposite to IKK inhibition.
No difference in response between lines with high vs. low constitutive NF-kB activity.

evidence.supports: PS1145 inhibits NF-kB activity and proliferation, and induces apoptosis in prostate carcinoma cells.
PS1145 inhibits proliferation of CML cell lines and primary bone marrow cells.
BAY 11-7082 induces cell death in multiple myeloma cells, though partly independent of NF-kB inhibition.
BMS-345541 reduces proliferation, induces apoptosis, and reverses EMT in prostate cancer cells.
BMS-345541 affects multiple mitotic cell cycle transitions, including mitotic entry and cytokinesis.
